metaDescription: Odoo Website in practice: multi-site and multi-language setup, the 301 redirect map, forms that create leads, cookie consent gaps and what Community covers.
intro: Odoo Website is a page builder that writes into the same database as the rest of the system. A page is a QWeb view holding the HTML plus a page record holding the URL, the published state and the menu entry. Nothing is exported to a separate CMS. That is the whole argument for using it: a form on a landing page creates a lead with its campaign attached, a product page reads live stock, and a portal login shows the customer their own invoices.

The builder is a Community app. Pages, blocks, the blog, the forum, multi-language including right to left, the SEO fields and multi-website all work on a Community licence. An Enterprise subscription buys the apps behind the pages rather than the pages themselves. Helpdesk tickets raised from a contact form, Marketing Automation for the follow up, Studio for adding a field without a developer and Sign are the parts people usually mean when they ask what the paid edition adds.

What it is not is a publishing platform. There is no editorial workflow, no scheduled publishing queue, no content versioning past an undo in the editor, and design freedom stops where the theme grid stops. A brand whose site is the product, or a newsroom with ten writers working in parallel, is better served by a front end of its own reading Odoo over the API. Most companies do not have that problem and should not pay for that answer.
whoFor: Companies whose site already produces enquiries that somebody is retyping into a spreadsheet or a CRM by hand.
B2B manufacturers and distributors who want a public catalogue, a request for quotation form and a customer portal running off one product list.
Groups selling into several markets who need a site per country, in the local language, without a separate CMS and a separate login for each one.
Marketing teams who need a landing page live on the day of the campaign rather than in the next development sprint.
Not for publishers and media sites that need editorial workflow, embargoes and several writers working on the same content at once.
Not for brands where the site is the product and a bespoke design system with a headless front end reading Odoo over the API is the honest answer.

capabilities.title: Where the content actually lives
capabilities.body: Blocks dragged onto a page are saved as HTML inside a view record. The URL, the published flag, the menu entry and the search indexing switch live on the page record beside it. Because content is a database row and not a file, it is backed up with the database, it is not in your git repository, and it does not move with a code deployment. Every decision further down this page follows from that one fact, so agree it before the first page is built.

capabilities.title: Several websites from one database
capabilities.body: One database can serve several websites, each with its own domain, theme, menus, languages, company and pricelists. Records carry a website reference, and a record left without one is shared by all of them. That is how a group runs a corporate site plus three country sites without three databases to upgrade and three product lists to maintain. The cost is that a view edited while one site is active becomes private to that site, so decide early which parts are meant to stay common.

capabilities.title: Languages and right to left
capabilities.body: Installing a language gives the site a URL prefix per language, a language selector and alternate hreflang links on translated pages. Arabic and Hebrew flip the layout and the stylesheet is generated in a mirrored version, so direction itself is not the hard part. Translation is per field and per block: a block added to the English page appears untranslated on the Arabic one until somebody writes it, and text baked into an image is never translated at all.

capabilities.title: Forms that write to real records
capabilities.body: The form block posts into a model rather than an inbox. Contact Us can create a lead, raise a Helpdesk ticket on Enterprise, or send a message. Fields map to model fields in the editor, required and hidden values are set there, and a model has to be marked as available to website forms before it can be chosen. Google reCAPTCHA v3 is a settings toggle. A lead created this way carries the campaign, source and medium it arrived with, which is what makes ad spend traceable.

capabilities.title: SEO controls that are per page, not global
capabilities.body: Each page has its own title, meta description, keywords, social preview image and an indexing toggle. Odoo emits a canonical link and alternate language links, generates sitemap.xml as a cached file rather than rebuilding it on each request, and exposes robots.txt as an editable view. Redirects are ordinary records: 301, 302 and rewrite rules kept under configuration. That table is where a legacy URL structure gets mapped during a migration, and it is searchable and exportable like any other list.

capabilities.title: Gated pages, visitors and the portal
capabilities.body: Page visibility can be set to everyone, signed in users, a named user group or a password, which turns a specification sheet or a price list into a gated asset without a plugin. Visitors are tracked as records showing the pages they viewed, and a visitor becomes a known contact the moment they log in or submit a form. Live chat, the blog and the forum all read the same visitor and contact records, so nobody maintains a second user table.

capabilities.title: Theme, brand and injected code
capabilities.body: The theme panel sets colours, fonts, header and footer layout and button styles across the whole site, and a designer can go further with SCSS delivered in a small module. Head and body code can be added per page for a tag manager or a chat widget. A CDN base URL can be configured so static assets are served from an edge network. Fonts should be hosted on your own domain rather than pulled from a third party if European visitors are in scope.

setup.title: Fix the URL structure and the redirect map first
setup.body: Before a block is dragged, list every URL on the old site with its traffic, decide its new address, and load the pairs as 301 records. Pull that list from the old sitemap and from Search Console, not from memory, because the pages that earn traffic are rarely the ones anyone remembers. A relaunch that goes live without redirects loses the rankings that justified the project, and recovery takes months rather than days.

setup.title: Set the domain, then freeze the base URL
setup.body: Each website record has a domain field and it needs the full address including the protocol, because canonical links, social previews and every link inside an outgoing email are built from it. The database also holds a base URL parameter that by default is rewritten to whatever host the last administrator logged in from. Set the freeze parameter on any database reachable on more than one hostname, or password reset emails start pointing at a staging server.

setup.title: Decide the language model before anyone translates
setup.body: Choose which languages are real, whether each market gets its own website record or a language prefix on a single one, and who owns the wording. A separate site per country allows different menus, prices, legal pages and contact details. A language on one site keeps the structure identical and swaps only the words. Arabic almost always needs the first option, because right to left layout, local contacts and a different page order are not a translation task.

setup.title: Wire forms to the model that owns the follow up
setup.body: Point the contact form at a lead with a sales team, a salesperson and a source set, rather than at a shared mailbox. Configure the required fields, switch on reCAPTCHA, and test both the acknowledgement to the sender and the notification to the team. Agree what happens to a submission that arrives at midnight. A form that creates a lead nobody owns is worse than a mail link, because everyone assumes it is being handled.

setup.title: Moving content off WordPress or a static site
setup.body: There is no importer, and anyone who says otherwise has not tried it. Pages are rebuilt as blocks, which is quick for a forty page brochure site and slow for a thousand post blog. Posts can be loaded into the blog model over the API, but the pasted HTML has to be reduced to the classes the editor understands or the first edit reflows the layout. Images move into the filestore and every path inside the content has to be rewritten.

pitfalls.title: Content does not travel with your code
pitfalls.body: On Odoo.sh, or any setup with a staging branch, a deployment moves modules and not pages. Text edited on staging stays on staging. The two workable patterns are editing production directly with new pages left unpublished until they are ready, or pulling a fresh copy of production down before a content sprint. Teams that build a whole new site on staging and expect a merge to publish it end up rebuilding it by hand under deadline.

pitfalls.title: Editing a shared view splits it per site
pitfalls.body: In a multi-website database, changing a header, a footer or any other shared view while one site is active creates a copy bound to that site. From then on that site stops receiving changes to the original, including fixes that arrive with a module update. The behaviour is deliberate and correct. It still surprises people during an upgrade, when one site keeps an old footer and nobody can find where it is defined.

pitfalls.title: The cookies bar is a notice, not a consent manager
pitfalls.body: Odoo can display a cookie bar from the website settings. It informs the visitor. It does not block analytics or advertising scripts before a choice is made, it does not offer per category options, and it does not store evidence of consent. In Germany, France and the UK that gap is exactly what a regulator writes up. Budget for a dedicated consent tool and load the tag manager behind it rather than in front of it.

pitfalls.title: Page weight from an unmanaged image library
pitfalls.body: Photographs arrive at full camera resolution and go straight into a block. The editor can resize and re-encode on upload, but only if somebody uses it. A ten block page with untouched images runs to several megabytes, which is invisible on office fibre and painful on a phone in Karachi or Cairo. Put a maximum file size in the content brief and test finished pages on a throttled connection before launch, not after the first bounce rate report.

pitfalls.title: Swapping the theme after launch
pitfalls.body: Installing a different theme rewrites the colour palette, the fonts and the default blocks, and customised header or footer views can be reset in the process. Do it once, at the start, on a copy of the database, with a backup taken first. The same discipline applies to the sample pages a theme ships with: demo content left published gets indexed, and prospects and competitors do find it.

worksWith: eCommerce, which is the same builder with a catalogue, checkout and a local payment provider added
CRM, so a form submission becomes a lead with its campaign, source and medium already filled in
Blog and Forum, both Community, for the long tail pages and question threads that earn search traffic
Live Chat, reading the same visitor record the rest of the site writes to
Events and eLearning, for registration and course pages that sell through the normal checkout
Email Marketing, with Marketing Automation on Enterprise for what happens after a form is submitted
Google Search Console, reCAPTCHA and a tag manager loaded behind a consent tool
Studio on Enterprise, when a form has to write into a model with fields that do not exist yet

regional.note: Arabic is the primary version, not a translation layer: right to left layout, Arabic contact details and a page order local readers expect. Form data falls under the PDPL administered by SDAIA, so consent wording and a deletion route are part of the build. An online store also registers on Maroof and shows its commercial registration, while ZATCA rules apply at checkout rather than to content pages.

Sites aimed at UAE buyers normally run Arabic and English side by side, and consumer prices are shown inclusive of the 5 percent VAT. Personal data collected by forms sits under Federal Decree-Law 45 of 2021, while entities in the DIFC or ADGM answer to their own data protection regimes instead. The e-invoicing programme touches the checkout, not the brochure pages.

Cookie consent follows KVKK and the Board guidance, which means explicit opt in for anything past strictly necessary, with VERBIS registration for most controllers. An online store registers with ETBIS and displays the badge. The larger constraint is hosting: tax documents may not be archived outside Turkiye, so a database serving both the site and e-Fatura has to sit in country.

Every page needs an Impressum under section 5 DDG, and non essential cookies need consent before they load under section 25 TDDDG, previously the TTDSG. Host your fonts yourself, because a German court treated loading Google Fonts from Google servers as a data protection breach. Consumer facing shops also fall under the BFSG accessibility act in force since 28 June 2025, which points at EN 301 549.

The CNIL position is that refusing cookies must be as easy as accepting, so a banner offering only an accept button is a finding rather than a grey area. Mentions legales are mandatory on the site, and the loi Toubon requires French for commercial content addressed to French consumers. Public sector bodies answer additionally to the RGAA accessibility framework.

Non essential cookies need consent under PECR, and the ICO has written to high traffic sites about banners that make rejecting harder than accepting. Consumer prices are displayed inclusive of 20 percent VAT under the Price Marking Order. The Equality Act makes accessibility a service obligation, and WCAG 2.2 AA is the reference an auditor uses even outside the public sector.

The DPDP Act brings notice and consent duties to any form collecting personal data, and the Consumer Protection e-commerce rules require the seller legal name, address and a named grievance officer to be published on the site. Reach depends on more than English, and most visits arrive on a mid range Android phone, so page weight decides the bounce rate more than the design does.

No data protection statute is in force yet, so the constraints here are practical rather than legal. Traffic is mobile and largely on 4G, which makes image weight and asset bundle size the first thing to fix. Urdu content needs a Nastaliq capable web font, since the usual fallback renders it in Naskh, and most enquiries still arrive on WhatsApp rather than through a form.

faqs.q: Do we need Enterprise for the website builder?
faqs.a: No. Website, Blog, Forum, eCommerce, Live Chat and multi-language including right to left are all Community. The builder itself is identical in both editions. Enterprise buys what sits behind the page: Helpdesk for tickets raised from a form, Marketing Automation for the follow up, Studio for adding fields without a developer, and Sign for the document that closes the deal.

faqs.q: Can we keep our existing site and use Odoo only for the back office?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is sometimes the right call, particularly where a marketing team is already productive in another stack. The join is the form: post submissions into Odoo over the API so a lead is created with its attribution intact. What you give up is the live catalogue, stock, pricelists and a customer portal running from the same records as your invoices.

faqs.q: Can one database run several websites on different domains?
faqs.a: Yes. Each website record has its own domain, theme, menus, languages, company and pricelists, and any record left without a website reference is shared across them. It is the normal setup for a group with country sites. Allow time to decide what stays common, because editing a shared header while one site is active copies that view to that site permanently.

faqs.q: Will we lose our search rankings when we relaunch?
faqs.a: Only if the URL map is skipped. Export the old URLs with their traffic, decide the new address for each one, and load the pairs as 301 records before go live. Keep the titles and descriptions of pages that already rank instead of rewriting everything at once. Rankings normally wobble for a few weeks and recover once the redirects are complete.

faqs.q: Is an Odoo site fast enough?
faqs.a: For a brochure or catalogue site, yes, provided somebody attends to it. Compress images on upload, keep the block count per page sensible, serve static assets from a CDN using the setting in website configuration, and run enough workers for the traffic you expect. The usual cause of a slow Odoo site is a five megabyte hero image, not the framework underneath it.

faqs.q: Does Odoo handle cookie consent to European standards?
faqs.a: Not on its own. The built in cookies bar is a notice: it does not block scripts before a choice, offers no per category options and keeps no record of consent. Use a dedicated consent platform, load analytics and advertising tags behind it, and host fonts on your own domain. This is the most common compliance gap on an Odoo site in Europe.

faqs.q: Can our marketing team edit pages without breaking things?
faqs.a: Yes for text, images, blocks and new pages, which is the point of the builder. Give them the website editor group rather than system administrator, agree that theme settings and shared header or footer views are out of scope, and take a database backup before a large content push. Structural work stays with whoever owns the site.

faqs.q: How well does Odoo handle Arabic and right to left?
faqs.a: The layout is the easy part. Both the interface and the public site flip, and the stylesheet is generated in a mirrored version. Content is the work: every block, every image with text inside it and every downloadable PDF is a separate job per language, and machine translated product copy is visible to a native reader. Plan Arabic as a build, not as a checkbox.
